## How it works

- [statement] GET returns results, links and totalCount. Auditors must account for pagination because totalCount can exceed the number of returned entries; pageNum starts at 1 and itemsPerPage defaults to 100, with a documented maximum of 500. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ops-manager/current/reference/api/api-keys/org/get-all-org-api-key-access-list.md · keywords: Ops Manager per-key API access-list lifecycle
- [statement] Delete an entry with DELETE /orgs/{ORG-ID}/apiKeys/{API-KEY-ID}/accessList/{ACCESS-LIST-ENTRY}; when a CIDR includes a slash, encode it as %2F. The documented successful example returns HTTP 204 No Content. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ops-manager/current/reference/api/api-keys/org/delete-one-org-api-key-access-list.md · keywords: Ops Manager per-key API access-list lifecycle
- [statement] Nutanix’s April 7 2026 NDB integration guidance requires NDB API-server and agent addresses in the Ops Manager access list for registration, and DB-server addresses for later association. Use this integration-specific caller inventory when planning access changes; the article does not identify the precise per-key endpoint. (low confidence) — https://www.nutanix.com/blog/onboarding-mongodb-ops-manager-in-nutanix-ndb · keywords: Ops Manager per-key API access-list lifecycle

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Avesha’s KubeSlice 1.4.0 walkthrough records HTTP 403 IP_ADDRESS_NOT_ON_ACCESS_LIST for operator address 10.6.0.5 during project discovery or creation. An apparent organization-not-found wrapper can therefore require checking the enclosed access-list error and actual caller address. (low confidence) — https://docs.avesha.io/documentation/open-source/1.4.0/use-cases/mongodb/distributed-mongodb-for-multicloud/ · keywords: Ops Manager per-key API access-list lifecycle

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The organization-key resource /orgs/{ORG-ID}/apiKeys/{API-KEY-ID}/accessList supports collection GET and POST, plus GET and DELETE for an individual entry; the endpoint overview lists no in-place update operation. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ops-manager/current/reference/api/org-api-key-access-lists.md · keywords: Ops Manager per-key API access-list lifecycle · also: https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/ops-manager@v0.63.0/opsmngr
- [statement] POST requires an array even for one entry. Each document supplies ipAddress or cidrBlock, mutually exclusively. New values are appended to existing entries; submitting the desired final list does not remove older entries. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ops-manager/current/reference/api/api-keys/org/create-org-api-key-access-list.md · keywords: Ops Manager per-key API access-list lifecycle
- [statement] Per-entry audit metadata includes created, count, lastUsed and lastUsedAddress. The last-use fields appear only after a request originates from the address; lastUsed has an access-related update condition, so an absent value is not evidence of a failed attempt. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ops-manager/current/reference/api/api-keys/org/get-all-org-api-key-access-list.md · keywords: Ops Manager per-key API access-list lifecycle · also: https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/ops-manager@v0.63.0/opsmngr
- [statement] Deleting an organization API key also removes its access from every project to which it was granted access; inventory project grants before retiring a key. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ops-manager/current/tutorial/manage-programmatic-api-keys.md · keywords: Ops Manager per-key API access-list lifecycle
